notes:
Summary: mid-market ecommerce platform doing real-time personalization + live chat. Very latency- and cost-sensitive — primary objective: keep user-facing SA chat p95 under 80ms and product recommendation latency under 40ms for cold-start flows. Heavy burst profile during flash sales (10x baseline qps for ~10 min).

Key requirements / asks:
- Workloads: low-latency chat (short-turn dialogue), per-request reranking for recommendations, on-the-fly embeddings for session context.
- Targets: chat p50~15ms, p95 <=80ms; rerank p50 <10ms, p95 <50ms; sustained throughput target 1k-1.5k qps with 10k peak bursts.
- Cost sensitivity: target cost per 1M tokens <$200 (hosted) or unit economics on Dedicated comparable to current infra.
- Routing: prefer local region routing (NA), automatic fallback to lower-cost quantized variants during heavy load.
- Interested in: intelligent batching (latency-aware batching), prefix/KV caching for session state, per-workload quantization profiles (8-bit/4-bit), and model selection policies that trade accuracy vs cost.
- Compliance: SOC2 required, SSO (SAML) integration must be complete before production, KMS integration and audit logs mandatory, data residency for EU customers (they have EU stores).

What we heard on calls (verbatim / paraphrase):
- "We can't accept 300ms p95 during flash sales — customers churn."
- "If you can show 30% token-cost savings with similar NLG quality, we will accelerate procurement."

POC plan (agreed):
1) Baseline run on their sample traffic (3 days) using hosted small model -> measure latency and cost.
2) Dedicated pool trial (3 nodes) with batch tuning + prefix cache enabled. Run stress test that simulates 10x flash sale peak.
3) Quantized model variants (4-bit, 8-bit) with quality evals over 500 prompt samples.
4) Deliver heatmap: p50/p95 latency vs qps vs config (batch size, cache TTL, quantization), and cost per 1M tokens.

Risks / Blockers:
- Procurement wanting a fixed price component for flash sale capacity — conflicts with Redwood burst billing model.
- Legal needs documented data residency flows for EU customers (explicit replication/processing notes).
- Engineering wants end-to-end perf trace (token-level) before signing — asked for tracing hooks in the console.
